implementation: ast-grep 0.37.0 structural rules; no Rust type or control-flow resolution

statuses.structural-subset: An executable pattern exists for a documented narrow syntax shape. This is not complete semantic enforcement.
statuses.existing-clippy-partial: Some existing Clippy checks are already configured; the whole policy is not proven.
statuses.deferred-semantic: No executable rule is claimed; the requirement remains code review until the stated analysis exists.

docDerivedRules.title: Use successful-commit test helpers
docDerivedRules.limits: Recognizes selected test match/extraction shapes. It does not resolve CommitResult, prove helper availability, or establish that success-arm checks/custom diagnostics can be removed.

source.quote: Use `txn.commit(engine)?.unwrap_committed()`

docDerivedRules.title: Use KernelResultIterator marker
docDerivedRules.limits: Recognizes selected explicit default-KernelResult + Send bound spellings. Aliases, generic error parameters, extra bounds and borrowed/dyn lifetimes need review.

source.quote: Prefer the `KernelResultIterator<T>` marker trait

docDerivedRules.title: Reuse canonical log-action fields and schemas
docDerivedRules.limits: Only the canonical Add-field reconstruction shape is implemented. Other action fields, complete LOG_* schemas and arbitrary projections are not checked for semantic equivalence.

source.quote: For Delta log action schemas, reuse the canonical

docDerivedRules.title: No function-local imports
docDerivedRules.limits: Checks use declarations syntactically nested inside functions. Macro token streams/expansions are not traversed; moving an import still needs resolution/collision review.

source.quote: Place `use` imports at the top of the file

docDerivedRules.title: Use equality for simple enum comparisons
docDerivedRules.limits: Recognizes selected simple unit-variant matches! syntax. It cannot prove PartialEq, resolved enum identity or evaluation/borrow equivalence.

source.quote: Prefer `==` over `matches!` for simple single-variant enum comparisons.

docDerivedRules.title: Name literal field nullability
docDerivedRules.limits: Recognizes named StructField::new calls with literal booleans. It cannot distinguish shadowed/Arrow types or exempt every constructor-under-test automatically.

source.quote: Prefer `StructField::nullable` / `StructField::not_null`

docDerivedRules.title: Use Into<DataType> at generic construction boundaries
docDerivedRules.limits: Recognizes Box-backed DataType constructor spellings. Passing a container directly at impl Into<DataType> boundaries requires parameter/type resolution and remains a reviewed decision.

source.quote: Leverage `impl Into<DataType>`

docDerivedRules.title: Use the right Result alias and envelope
docDerivedRules.limits: Recognizes an explicit Result/KernelError alias spelling. It cannot select Error envelopes, rewrite third-party trait contracts, or prove generic error conversion behavior.

source.quote: Kernel APIs use `KernelResult<T, E = KernelError>`

docDerivedRules.title: Use documented expression shorthand
docDerivedRules.limits: Covers selected lit/null_lit, static boolean-predicate and simple col! patterns. Runtime values, typed Predicate::NULL inference, aliases and constructor tests need review.

source.quote: When building expressions inline, prefer `lit(value)` and `null_lit(data_type)`

docDerivedRules.title: Use schema literals with matching validation
docDerivedRules.limits: Only a narrow trusted single-field unchecked-schema literal pattern is implemented. General schema_ref!/lazy_schema_ref!/try_schema! rewrites and checked nested validation are not proven.

source.quote: Prefer the `schema!` / `schema_ref!` macros

docDerivedRules.title: No production panics
docDerivedRules.limits: Existing Kernel configuration warns on three Clippy panic-related lints outside cfg(test). It does not establish absence of all production panics, including indexing/arithmetic and other macros.

source.quote: NEVER panic in production code: use errors instead.

docDerivedRules.title: Keep EngineData opaque outside engine adapters
docDerivedRules.limits: Path-scoped ArrowEngineData downcast shapes are checked. Other concrete types, aliases, engine-adapter boundaries and indirect downcasts are not type-resolved.

source.quote: **EngineData is opaque:** inspect rows through the visitor APIs.

docDerivedRules.title: Do not assume one batch per file
docDerivedRules.limits: No executable check. Correct single-next use depends on the file-reader contract, remaining iterator uses and whether the caller intentionally probes or short-circuits.

source.quote: NEVER assume one batch per file: ALWAYS iterate.

docDerivedRules.deferredReason: No executable check. Correct single-next use depends on the file-reader contract, remaining iterator uses and whether the caller intentionally probes or short-circuits.

source.quote: `arrow::array::new_null_array(&arrow_type, n)`

docDerivedRules.title: No Rust-reference parameters in new C APIs
docDerivedRules.limits: Checks Rust reference types in selected extern C signatures under ffi/src. It is not an ABI migration, diff analysis, or a proof of pointer validity/lifetimes/ownership.

docDerivedRules.title: No new unsafe in Miri-ignored tests
docDerivedRules.limits: Checks unsafe blocks under the exact cfg_attr(miri, ignore) attribute shape. The baseline detects new matched syntax, but cannot prove indirect Miri coverage or arbitrary added-unsafe semantics.

source.quote: Never add new `unsafe` to a Miri-ignored test.

userSupplementedRules.title: Prefer column_name! for known simple paths
userSupplementedRules.limits: Only selected simple literal segment sequences are candidates. Constants, runtime strings, dotted single-segment names and aliases are deliberately not inferred.

userSupplementedRules.title: Prefer named predicate and fluent constructors
userSupplementedRules.limits: Selected named/fluent Predicate constructor spellings are matched. No type resolution or proof about AST normalization, numeric types, aliases or operand effects is provided.

userSupplementedRules.title: Prefer arithmetic operators and semantic expression builders
userSupplementedRules.limits: Selected arithmetic and named-variadic constructors are matched. The lhs must resolve to Kernel Expression and preserve the same AST; primitive arithmetic and runtime operator dispatch are not equivalent.

userSupplementedRules.title: Encourage expr! for supported composed literal trees
userSupplementedRules.limits: No executable general expr! rewrite. expr! returns Expression, has a constrained grammar, and may normalize wrappers/junctions. Composed-tree rewrites remain semantic review.
userSupplementedRules.deferredReason: No executable general expr! rewrite. expr! returns Expression, has a constrained grammar, and may normalize wrappers/junctions. Composed-tree rewrites remain semantic review.

userSupplementedRules.title: Prefer module-scope imports over inline crate paths
userSupplementedRules.limits: Use Clippy's existing absolute_paths lint in the advisory profile rather than duplicating it with an AST rule. Rust 1.100's default absolute-paths-max-segments=2 diagnoses crate::module::Type; setting it to 1 also diagnoses crate::Root. The builtin covers other absolute paths, including std paths, and follows Clippy's own exceptions; it is broader than a crate-only policy. Intentional qualification remains a reviewed Clippy allowance. No custom AST rule or baseline findings are added for this preference.

userSupplementedRules.title: Name if/match results before passing them to calls
userSupplementedRules.limits: Syntax-only review candidate for if/if-let and match in direct call arguments, including parentheses, references and ? wrappers. Ancestor matching stops at all other expressions: closure/block arguments, receivers, branches, loops, binary/await/cast expressions and signature/type contexts are not traversed. A direct argument of an inner call inside a closure still diagnoses. Macro definitions/invocations, attributes, comments and strings are excluded. No automatic replacement: preserve earlier-argument order, conditional execution, ? propagation and temporary/drop behavior when introducing locals.

additionalRules.limits: Recognizes explicitly spelled Result<Vec<_>> collection. No type resolution: aliases, collection inference, closure error constraints and unstable method-name collisions require review. No automatic replacement is provided.

Provides a replacement only when a direct file-level Itertools import exists. It does not prove that collect is the standard iterator method or that the Vec materialization is necessary. Run unnecessary-collection checks first; compile reviewed replacements.

Requires a same-named function parameter explicitly written impl KernelResultIterator<T>; does not infer generic bounds or aliases. It does not resolve local shadowing or mapping-function capture/evaluation equivalence.

Recognizes an immediately joined temporary Vec and a string-literal separator. Review item Display/Borrow equivalence, imports and destruction timing. A retained or reused Vec is deliberately not matched.

Specialized field_names().cloned().collect().join() suggestion. A reviewer must confirm Kernel StructType::field_names returns borrowed Strings; similarly named methods are not resolved by AST matching.

Flags only explicit Result::ok / Result::into_iter error-erasing adapters. It intentionally does not flag generic flatten() or Option pipelines. Intentional best-effort processing may keep the code with an explicit policy; different result-preserving adapters are not interchangeable fixes.

Recognizes directly collected fallible pairs immediately consumed by unzip. The equivalent process_results consumer drains input, but output inference, allocation layout and partial-value Drop order need semantic review.

Recognizes a two-element let-else slice pattern over split(char).collect::<Vec<_>>(). Review source type and iterator purity: collect_tuple checks exact arity but consumes fewer excess items. Reject extra delimiters as before; split_once alone is not equivalent.

Recognizes a narrow Ok/Err match retaining every error. Review Result constructor resolution, Itertools availability and mapping-function captures before using the supplied replacement. Side-effectful match arms do not match.

Consecutive test assertions with one shared binding and a literal/simple expected message only. Add the proper unit/integration helper import. Preserve is_err-only checks, exact/variant/multi-message checks and custom diagnostics. Warning spans the first statement; no automatic deletion/rewrite is offered.

Test-only candidate requiring an Arrow RecordBatch/StructArray receiver and concrete array type. Keep typed/value/null/schema/order assertions after lookup and custom diagnostics. Name is constrained to a literal; verify the receiver/type and macro import before fixing.

Review-only: this test function pretty-prints batches and normalizes a Vec of complete trim().lines() before sorting. Confirm the same table rendering and ignored row/batch order before using the shared macro. Expected lines must remain sorted separately. Keep typed/schema/null/order/batch-boundary assertions and custom filtered-row comparisons.

baselinePolicy: Existing findings are accepted by an explicit post-fix baseline. New unmatched diagnostic fingerprints/counts fail check unless locally suppressed with a reason or explicitly accepted by a reviewed refresh. Baseline acceptance is not proof of correctness.
fixPolicy: All current metadata has safeFix=false. Replacement previews require an exact reviewed manifest; scan/check never rewrite source.
notCovered: Workflow/documentation prose outside these 26 audited coding/test conventions is not claimed as enforced. Fixture-backed AST matching does not prove aliases, types, ownership, runtime configuration, complete call graphs or ABI correctness.
